title: AI usage in game development
author: Both-Consequence-989
selftext:
Hello!  
Quick dilemma so i wanted to find somewhere to ask and this seems like the right spot.   
TLDR: 

I'm in the middle of designing the bone structure and meat for a game I want to create. I myself though have no artistical capabilities. I have an idea, and can build it (i think, still picking the engine I want to use), so im head asking around to those I know if they can do pixel art styles, and skill sets.

I asked someone I know if they can do some art demos or "mock ups" for the game, and I noted the style and such to them.

  
While discussing the style and creation of the sprites I want to use, he mentioned something about "generating it with AI"  or "using AI to tweak the art" and then he himself would make it his own in illustrator or something like that. 

When I asked if he could do the art or sprites entirely by hand or manually in an art program he has, I received what can only be described as a plethora of excuses as to why that takes forever and how a first time game should be easy and such. Even noted I should have AI create my game for me and then just "shave off the fat" in not so many words.

Felt odd... and not what I wanted to do for my first game. 

Is this normal? Do game artists just slam ideas into an AI, have it generate basic concepts, and then tweak it from there? I'm not asking for Picasso style pixel art either. my games beekeeping related lol. I was just looking for effort in my art work for my game, to some degree. 

I've always gone under the premise of "fair work for fair pay". If you want me to pay you the top amount you want, I expect you to put effort in. Not have AI do the work and you just tidy it up.

Is there a area or place I can go to and reach out to other artists and such? I'm still new to game development, so any info is welcome.

comments.author: AdminClown
comments.body: AI is a tool. It’s a technology and it won’t disappear just because people don’t like it. Use it as a way to achieve your creative vision, not as a substitute.

replies.author: Both-Consequence-989
replies.body: Ok so that's fine. But isn't AI more of a tool that derives from accuracy, not creation? Like, Id use AI to help clean up code. Where is the line that's its acceptable to use AI for something it's not meant for? Like using a hammer to apply paint to a wall concept.

replies.author: AdminClown
replies.body:
There is no line where it's acceptable or not to use AI. If you want one, the line is the output.

Is the final output and result an accurate representation of what you had envisioned?

Or is it something that is a rough approximation that was the result of pure uncontrolled chaotic attempts with little to no effort to control it where you just laid it on the model and told it "give me whatever you can do best generate me ideas" and didn't bother to refine or change anything you didn't like?

EDIT: I personally am not satisfied with the current generative art aspect and or capabilities of AI, therefore I do not use it for more than just references to be interpreted in some aspect or another then discarded.

replies.author: CulveDaddy
replies.body: What is it not meant for?

replies.author: AdHom
replies.body: Software development, in the industry overall, is no longer based on writing the majority of code by hand. It is almost all AI written. It's simply not a good use of time for developers, and public opposition to AI is largely based on 1) arguments about artistic integrity that don't really apply to code, or 2) much less informed than the people saying it think, with most of it based on outdated word of mouth reports rather than actual personal experience.

comments.author: MelodramaticShape
comments.body: If you don't want them to use AI, make it clear in your contract that you don't want them to use AI. Problem solved. Don't have a contract? Get one.

comments.author: ValeriiKambarov
comments.body:
I can make you the style you need by hand without using AI. If, of course, it will be interesting for you.

You should realise that today a lot of people got into this area who only know how to use II. This is because it is sponsored and encouraged by a huge amount of money from large companies. So, sometime it will be really hard to find something else

comments.author: lazd
comments.body: I feel like paying artists to make art, by hand, for your game while writing some of the code with AI is a fair tradeoff. I’m an engineer and it took me a long time to warm up to AI for development, but I am still against it for art.

comments.author: sterneplatzen
comments.body:
I think it's normal for you to expect that level of effort, but you have to be communicating this to your artist and making sure that you are compensating them properly.

It's all about the workflow you choose and design philosophies that feel right to you.

Ask your artist to clarify his process and if it does not align, simply state that you'd prefer if the idea generation and main art illustration comes from them directly and have AI do touch ups instead of letting it drive the whole process.

There are plenty of artists available out there who are willing to provide documentation of their creative process showing that they made their work without AI or very minimal AI usage. You do not have to stay with this artist if it does not align with your vision.

comments.author: Halloween_Forever_
comments.body: Hey, uh. It's going to be difficult to find a forum to give you the actual advice you want because this has become a polarizing topic. Every forum is going to lean more one way or the other.

comments.author: QcyqApps
comments.body: You can check my posts and feedback from users. Players don’t like generative AI. It’s still your choice.
